1._section_summary: This abstract describes a single study investigating a model of positive body image with 249 college women. The study used path analysis to examine how body appreciation mediates the relationship between interpersonal/intrapersonal variables (caregiver eating messages, attachment, perfectionism) and outcomes (intuitive eating, depressive symptoms). Body appreciation was found to be a significant mediator, positively predicting intuitive eating but not depressive symptoms.

2._section_summary: This section describes the statistical testing of a hypothesized structural model with 249 participants using Mplus Version 4.1 and maximum likelihood estimation. The analysis examined relationships among variables including restrictive/critical caregiver eating messages, attachment anxiety, depressive symptoms, body appreciation, and intuitive eating, with BMI controlled for in the model. The final revised model demonstrated good fit indices (CFI=.99, SRMR=.04, RMSEA=.03) and revealed that body appreciation was predicted by multiple factors and in turn predicted intuitive eating.
